note: Decision trees for opening, managing, rolling, closing and taking losses on premium-selling trades. Nodes: decision (a question), action (do this), info (how it works). Management rules are CONVENTIONS: they reshape the P&L distribution and capital turnover; they do not add expected return [lit:williams-1991].

nodes.text: Is the symbol liquid? Check bid-ask width, open interest and volume together, at the strike and the symbol level.
If one strike is illiquid, move strikes or expiration; if the whole symbol is illiquid, skip it.
Is IV rank high? Above 50 favors selling premium; 20 or below favors buying or defined-risk.
Caveat: in our 1990-2026 test, high IV rank days had a slightly smaller average IV-RV spread and a far worse tail than low IV rank days.
Choose the strategy from your market assumption and the IV environment (see the strategy cards).
Pick duration: about 45 DTE for short premium, longer (60-65) when IV is low.
Size it: keep each trade under about 5% of the account; keep total options buying power in the 25-50% band (max 75%).
Enter as one multi-leg limit order, priced near the mid; a market order trades price control for speed.
Know the expiration date, time and settlement of the product before opening (SPX monthlies AM-settled, weeklies PM; equity options physically settled).
Has the trade reached its profit target? 50% of max profit for most short-premium trades; 10-50% for calendars, diagonals and iron flies; 25% of the debit for calendars.
Close it and redeploy the capital into a new trade.
Is it at or below about 21 DTE?
Close or roll to the next cycle rather than hold into expiration week.
Hold; check again.
Do not close for a tiny gain that commissions would eat (e.g. $0.10).
Effect: the 50% target raises the win rate and P&L per day, lowers P&L per trade; the 21-DTE exit cuts the worst-5% loss. Neither raises the expected return of the book.

trees.title: Defending and rolling a tested trade

nodes.text: Is one side tested (price at or through a short strike)?
Two-sided trades (strangle, iron condor): roll the untested side closer to the price for extra credit; a condor's untested side can go as far as the tested strike (an iron fly).
Can the trade be rolled out in time for a net credit?
Roll out for a credit, ideally 7-21 days before expiration; strikes may move closer only if the roll still brings a credit.
Do not roll for a debit: it worsens the breakeven and opens a low-probability trade. Close or keep the position under the loss rule instead.

Evidence: a roll is a close plus a new trade; the realized loss is real, and rolling the untested side adds exposure in the losing direction. Treat every roll as a new trade under the same size and stress limits.
Small accounts cannot keep rolling losers as long as large ones; keep individual trades small.
Has the net loss reached 2x the credit received (e.g. $1.00 collected, option now worth $3.00)?
tastylive: close the trade.

Evidence: in our strangle model a 2x-credit stop lowered the mean (+0.21 vs +0.26 credits a trade) and left the worst-5% average about unchanged, but it cut the single worst trade in the March 2020 crash from -28.8 to -4.7 credits. Closes-only data flatter it (real stop fills slip in spikes). Use it to cap disaster risk, not to add return.
Defined-risk trade?
Max loss was known at entry; many traders size it and let it run rather than stop out.
Undefined-risk: follow the loss rule or the roll-for-credit tree; never add size to a loser to recover.
Is a short option in the money or near the strike going into expiration?
Close it (or the whole spread) before expiration: a narrow spread where one leg is exercised and the other expires can turn small defined risk into a large share position.

ITM options at expiration convert to 100 shares per contract (short put -> long stock, short call -> short stock); OTM options expire worthless. Assignment notices arrive after the close, at random among writers.
Short ITM call on a stock going ex-dividend, with the dividend larger than the call's remaining extrinsic value?
Expect early assignment: close or roll the call before the ex-date.
European-style, cash-settled index options (SPX, XSP) cannot be assigned early and settle to cash; equity and ETF options are American-style and deliver shares.
Taxes (educational): broad index options fall under Section 1256 (60% long-term / 40% short-term); short-option gains are short-term; wash sales can apply across stock and options within 30 days.
Day trading: the tastylive page still describes the $25,000 pattern-day-trader rule; FINRA replaced it with intraday margin standards effective 2026-06-04 (brokers may phase in to 2027-10-20).
